contracts.title: Rational inverse Galois problem and dated status
exact_locators: Huang et al. v2, §1.1, printed pp.1–2
contracts.result_used: For each finite group G, seek a finite Galois field extension L/Q with Gal(L/Q) isomorphic to G. The general assertion remains open in the checked 2026 sources.
hypotheses: G is any finite abstract group; base is Q.

notation_dictionary.L: an actual field, finite over Q

contracts.application_check: A representation on a vector space, a G-action on a disconnected algebra, or a realization over a larger base is not by itself the requested field extension.
exceptions_or_caveats: This is a dated source check, not an exhaustive certification that no subsequent paper exists. The newer v2 status context was inspected on 9 October 2026.

contracts.title: Regular realization is a stronger input
exact_locators: Introduction, printed p.71, zero-based PDF p.0
contracts.result_used: A regular realization over k is a Galois field extension of k(t) in which k is algebraically closed. Over a Hilbertian base it implies an ordinary realization.
hypotheses: Finite Galois extension; characteristic zero is the project scope.
contracts.application_check: Regularity excludes new algebraic constants; the symbol t is transcendental.
exceptions_or_caveats: An ordinary realization does not furnish a regular one by adjoining a dummy variable. For nontrivial L/Q, L(t)/Q(t) contains L as new constants.
No converse from ordinary to regular realization is asserted.

contracts.title: Hilbert specialization with a controlled exceptional locus
exact_locators: Dèbes notes, Theorem 2.6.3(a),(d), printed p.85; Remark 2.6.5, p.87
Dèbes notes, Definition 5.2.2 and Theorem 5.2.4, p.206; Proposition 5.2.14, pp.213–214
contracts.source_status: proves theorem and corollary; modern paper states the regular consequence
contracts.result_used: Over Q, a finite Galois extension of Q(t_1,...,t_r) admits specializations retaining G on a Hilbert subset outside a proper Zariski closed exceptional locus. A fixed nonzero constraint polynomial may also be kept nonzero.
hypotheses: r ≥ 1; finite Galois field extension; a primitive polynomial for the full extension, not merely for an arbitrary smaller root field; localization avoids coefficients, denominators and discriminant zeros.

notation_dictionary.P: minimal polynomial of a primitive element of the entire Galois extension

contracts.application_check: The specialized primitive polynomial stays irreducible of degree |G|. Away from the model exceptional locus its splitting-field group embeds into G. Equality of degrees forces the full group. Zariski density permits replacing finitely many nonzero restrictions by their product.
exceptions_or_caveats: Characteristic zero alone is insufficient: Q is Hilbertian by the cited theorem; C is not.
For one parameter the excluded polynomial zero set is finite. In several parameters it is generally an infinite proper hypersurface.
Not every unbranched value retains the full group. Infinitely many suitable values need not, without a separate argument, describe distinct isomorphism classes for a nonregular constant extension.
For a nontrivial regular one-parameter extension, Huang et al. state infinitely many G-extensions over Q. The trivial group is handled separately.
The author lecture notes are a work in progress and have unfinished cross references. The locally pinned numbered statements, rather than dangling references, were used.

contracts.title: Shafarevich solvable-group realization
contracts.result_used: For a global field k and a finite solvable group G, some finite Galois K/k has Gal(K/k) isomorphic to G.
hypotheses: Take k=Q; G finite and solvable.
contracts.application_check: This supplies an external existence theorem for the solvable sector.
exceptions_or_caveats: This theorem does not by itself prescribe arbitrary completions, bound discriminants, give a polynomial algorithm, or prove regular realization over Q(t).
The authors explicitly correct a prime 2 issue in the original Shafarevich argument. The corrected proof source is used rather than treating the 1954 article alone as the extracted complete proof.

contracts.title: Every symmetric group is realizable over Q
exact_locators: Theorem 4.28, p.69; Lemma 4.31 and Example 4.32, pp.70–71
contracts.result_used: Every S_n occurs over Q. Squarefree modular patterns, irreducibility, and an elementary permutation criterion provide a construction.
hypotheses: n ≥ 1; n=1 and n=2 are handled separately; for n≥3 use a monic integral polynomial with the required squarefree reductions.

notation_dictionary.G_f: group of the splitting field, not of a single root field

contracts.application_check: The authors may prove their own subgroup criterion. The external arithmetic step is LC08. A full S_n splitting field has degree n!, not n.
exceptions_or_caveats: The source prints 15f_1+10f_2+6f_3 for monic degree-n polynomials. Its leading coefficient is 31. To retain the monic input of Theorem 4.28, use coefficientwise monic CRT or subtract 30X^n. All reductions mod2, mod3, mod5 are unchanged by that subtraction.
Repeated low-degree factors must be excluded when making modular patterns.

contracts.title: Cyclotomic Galois group
contracts.result_used: Gal(Q(ζ_N)/Q) is (Z/NZ)^× through σ(ζ_N)=ζ_N^a. Finite multiplicative subgroups of a field are cyclic.
hypotheses: N ≥ 1; ζ_N primitive. For the arbitrary-base injection, the characteristic must not divide N.
contracts.application_check: For prime p the cyclotomic group is cyclic of order p−1.
exceptions_or_caveats: For arbitrary K the exponent map may be a proper subgroup of the unit group. The isomorphism here is specifically over Q.
Exponentiation describes the automorphism on roots of unity, not on every field element.

contracts.title: Cyclic fixed-field construction
exact_locators: Conrad Patterns in Primes, Theorem 2.4, printed p.2
contracts.result_used: For m>1, choose a prime p≡1 modm and let H be the subgroup of order (p−1)/m in Gal(Q(ζ_p)/Q). Its fixed field has group C_m.
hypotheses: m is a positive integer; take Q for m=1.

notation_dictionary.p: cyclotomic conductor, which need not equal m
notation_dictionary.H: kernel of the cyclic quotient of order m

contracts.application_check: The quotient computation and normality of H are elementary project deductions.
exceptions_or_caveats: Dirichlet is stated, not proved, in the author notes. No effective search bound follows. The piece can use only C2/C3 examples without importing this general prime existence step.

An optional elementary Φ_m(m) construction and a Gaussian period generator are recorded in classical_constructions_check.json. They are optional and not dependencies of the manuscript unless written out and audited.

contracts.title: Good-prime factor degrees give a cycle
exact_locators: Theorem 4.28, printed p.69, zero-based PDF p.78
contracts.result_used: For monic f∈Z[X] and prime p with squarefree reduction, its distinct irreducible factor degrees modulo p are the cycle lengths of some element of Gal(f/Q).
hypotheses: Monic integral polynomial; p does not divide disc(f), equivalently the reduction has simple roots.

notation_dictionary.G_f: permutations of roots in the characteristic-zero splitting field

contracts.application_check: For x^4−x−1, the independent exact computation must verify the mod2 and mod7 factorizations and squarefreeness before supplying 4-cycle and 3+1-cycle witnesses. The theorem is the bridge from those finite factorizations to the characteristic-zero group.
exceptions_or_caveats: Finite modular data alone does not prove the bridge.
A cycle witness gives an element in the actual Galois group, not every permutation having the same cycle shape.

contracts.title: Irreducible cubic discriminant classification over Q
exact_locators: Corollary 4.2, p.58; Proposition 4.5, p.59; Example 4.7, p.60
contracts.result_used: An irreducible cubic over Q has group A_3≅C_3 if its discriminant is a square, and S_3 otherwise.
hypotheses: Cubic irreducible over Q, hence separable; discriminant is nonzero.

notation_dictionary.G_f: splitting-field group acting transitively on three roots

contracts.application_check: Irreducibility and the exact discriminant must be separately established for each worked cubic.
exceptions_or_caveats: Corollary 4.2 requires characteristic ≠2. Example 4.7 prints characteristic ≠3, which is insufficient for its square criterion in characteristic2. The project uses Q only, so both exclusions hold.

contracts.title: Artin finite automorphism fixed-field theorem
exact_locators: Corollary 3.11, printed pp.45–46; underlying Theorem 3.4 and Corollary 3.5, pp.42–43
contracts.result_used: For a finite subgroup G⊂Aut(E) of a field, E/E^G is finite Galois with group G and degree |G|.
hypotheses: E is a field; the given action is faithful, so G is actually embedded in Aut(E).
contracts.application_check: Permutation of algebraically independent variables induces distinct Q-automorphisms. This proves realization over the invariant field.
exceptions_or_caveats: It does not prove E^G=Q or E^G purely transcendental. A unitary representation alone supplies no field multiplication.

contracts.title: Ordinary Galois correspondence
contracts.result_used: For finite Galois E/F, H↦E^H reverses subgroup inclusion. Normal H gives Gal(E^H/F)≅G/H.
hypotheses: The ambient field extension is already finite Galois.
contracts.application_check: Intersection and compositum translations used in the packet lattice are deductions from this correspondence.
exceptions_or_caveats: The finite-dimensional projector range can represent the fixed vector space. Multiplication and the ambient Galois field still need to be supplied to identify it with a fixed field.

contracts.title: Finite normal basis theorem
contracts.result_used: A finite Galois E/F has a basis consisting of the G-conjugates of one element.
hypotheses: Finite Galois extension; the source uses finite in Definition 3.9.

notation_dictionary.F[G]→E: Σ a_g g ↦ Σ a_g g(α)

contracts.application_check: This gives an equivariant F-vector-space isomorphism with the regular module.
exceptions_or_caveats: The isomorphism is not an algebra isomorphism with the group algebra. Transported field multiplication depends on the chosen field and normal basis. No field is created from a regular module by this theorem.

contracts.title: Field trace, norm and towers
contracts.source_status: proves for separable extensions; leaves inseparable tower case as exercise
contracts.result_used: In a finite Galois extension, trace is Σ_g g(x), norm is ∏_g g(x). Both compose through intermediate field towers.
hypotheses: Finite separable extension for the project; finite Galois where the sum/product is over the full group.
contracts.application_check: In characteristic zero, P_H(x)=Tr_(L/L^H)(x)/|H|. The norm is multiplicative and nonlinear as a map of vector spaces.
exceptions_or_caveats: A normalized projector is the trace divided by group order, not the unnormalized trace. Do not assert norm is a linear transfer.
In positive characteristic dividing |H| the normalized formula is not available.

contracts.title: Noether rationality is sufficient, not automatic
contracts.source_status: states strategy and reports negative background
contracts.result_used: If Q(x_g)^G is purely transcendental over Q, the finite Galois invariant-field extension can be Hilbert-specialized to realize G over Q.
hypotheses: Faithful field action as in LC10; an actual Q-field rational parametrization of the invariant field; finite number of parameters.
contracts.application_check: Transport the finite Galois extension across the rational field isomorphism and apply LC03.
exceptions_or_caveats: Milne’s Aside 5.41 reports Swan’s 1969 negative example for the cyclic group of order 47. That report is background only: the project has not independently audited Swan’s paper or proof, and the negative example is not a proof dependency.
Failure of that sufficient rationality route does not refute inverse Galois realizability of the group.
The manuscript does not use this source to claim every invariant field is rational or that a representation repair proves the missing rationality hypothesis.

contracts.title: Continuous finite quotients of the absolute Galois group
exact_locators: Theorem 7.13, statement on printed pp.125–126, especially (b) and (d)
contracts.result_used: Restriction Gal(Ω/F)→Gal(L/F) is a continuous surjection when L/F is a finite Galois intermediate extension. A continuous homomorphism q:Gal(Ω/F)→E to a finite discrete group has an open normal kernel H; M=Ω^H is finite Galois over F and Gal(M/F)≅Gal(Ω/F)/H≅im(q).
hypotheses: Ω/F is Galois and carries the Krull topology; E is finite with the discrete topology; q is a continuous group homomorphism. For the project take F=Q and Ω=Qbar.

notation_dictionary.q: the proposed lift to the finite group E
notation_dictionary.M=Ω^H: finite Galois field supplied by the correspondence

contracts.application_check: Chapter 6 has a continuous lift q with π∘q=ρ, where ρ is restriction to L. Then ker(q)⊆ker(ρ), so the order-reversing correspondence gives L⊆M. For a surjective lift, the identified group is E, and restriction to L becomes π; its kernel gives Gal(M/L)≅ker(π). The weak case supplies im(q), not necessarily E.
exceptions_or_caveats: An abstract homomorphism is insufficient without continuity. Openness follows from the finite discrete target and continuity, while normality follows from being a kernel.
This correspondence turns an already constructed continuous quotient into a finite field. It does not prove a proper lift exists for every embedding problem.
The first isomorphism theorem and the kernel inclusion are elementary project deductions, rather than extra existence theorems.

contracts.title: Primitive elements for finite characteristic-zero realizations
contracts.result_used: If E=F[α_1,...,α_r] is finite over F and α_2,...,α_r are separable over F, then E=F[γ] for some γ. In particular every finite separable field extension has a primitive element.
hypotheses: Finite field extension, with a finite generating list satisfying the separability condition; all algebraic generators are separable in characteristic zero. The project uses a finite Galois extension of Q.

notation_dictionary.γ: the primitive element used in the polynomial certificate
notation_dictionary.Q[γ]: the whole extension, not merely a subfield

contracts.application_check: The degree of the minimal polynomial of γ is [L:Q]=|G| for an existing G-realization. The power basis 1,γ,...,γ^(|G|−1) gives a unique rational expression for each automorphism image of γ, so the certificate format in Chapter 7 can encode any existing realization. These degree and basis assertions are the project’s elementary consequences of the source theorem.
exceptions_or_caveats: Existence of a primitive element for an already given finite separable extension is not a procedure to construct a realization of an arbitrary group.
No claim is made that a generator of an arbitrary smaller root field generates the full splitting field.
The source theorem is slightly stronger than the separable special case: its first generator need not be separable. Only the characteristic-zero special case is used.
